title: Sociocultural Approach Adventure 1: Social Identity Theory
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet Tajfel & Turner's Social Identity Theory (1979).
meta_desc: Psychology Sociocultural: Social Identity Theory (Tajfel & Turner 1979) and minimal group paradigm.
final_note: You explained SIT and the in-group/out-group bias from minimal group studies.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Tajfel & Turner (1979) proposed three cognitive steps.

1. Social categorisation — sort self and others into groups.
2. Social identification — adopt the in-group's identity and norms.
3. Social comparison — compare favourably to out-group to raise self-esteem.

Tajfel et al. (1971) sorted Bristol schoolboys by trivial criteria (preferring Klee or Kandinsky).

Despite no interaction, participants allocated money to favour in-group over out-group — even sacrificing absolute payoff to maximise the gap.

SIT helps explain sports rivalries, nationalism, sectarian conflict, organisational silos.

Reducing bias: recategorisation (one super-ordinate group), contact hypothesis (Allport 1954, supported by Pettigrew & Tropp 2006 meta-analysis).
